description_full: Airtel Africa Plc, together with its subsidiaries, provides telecommunications and mobile money services in Nigeria, East Africa, and Francophone Africa. It offers pre and post-paid wireless voice, international roaming, and fixed line telephony services; data services, including 4G and 5G, home broadband, fibre, and data centers; and mobile money services, such as digital wallet payments systems, microloans, merchant, savings, insurance, international, and international money transfers. The company also provides messaging, value added, and tower sharing services, as well as infrastructure sharing, mobile commerce, and support services. The company was incorporated in 2018 and is based in London, the United Kingdom. Airtel Africa Plc is a subsidiary of Airtel Africa Mauritius Limited.

financial_summary: Airtel Africa Plc is a large-cap communication services business with a $15.0B market cap on $6.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 16% against a 8% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 70% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $2.3B in free cash flow — roughly 36 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.71× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -18.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.7× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 2.7× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 169 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 118% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 22% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 21% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 145% and a beta of 0.86, it moves roughly with the market.

val: The stock trades 75% below its DCF fair value of $164, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 45%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $116 to $240 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Communication Services peers: cheaper on P/FCF 6.5 vs 11.3, richer on P/E 20.1 vs 14.9 and EV/EBITDA 48.0 vs 9.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 15.5% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 1.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 8.1% annual cash-flow growth, 20pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 16% clears the cost of capital of 8.4% by 8pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.37).
It runs a 70% gross margin and converts 36% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: a Piotroski score of 9/9 and cash conversion of 4.71x, but high accruals (-18.0% of assets).
ROE of 22% is amplified by 4.4x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
SG&A jumped 32% last year, worth watching.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.7x net debt to EBITDA ($878.0M of cash against $6.4B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, and interest cover is thin at 2.7x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.64 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
The value-trap profile is elevated (52/100); see the breakdown below.
The current ratio of 0.58 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 6.9% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: It returns 2.1% a year to shareholders (0.5% in buybacks and 2.1% in dividends).
people: With about 4,512 employees, each generates about $1.4M of revenue, 2.3x the Communication Services median.
